name: Tokyo Disneyland
nameLocal: 東京ディズニーランド
kidNotes: Under-4s enter free. Fantasyland is perfect for 3–6 year olds; rope-drop it before the queues build.
summary: The classic Disney park with a distinctly Japanese polish — immaculate, gentle, and magical at Christmas when the parade lights up the castle.
tncTip: Go on a weekday, be at the gate by 8:30, and plan a midday hotel nap. We came back for the parade refreshed instead of melting down.

booking.howTo: Dated tickets open 60 days ahead at 2 PM Japan time and are sold online only — there are no tickets at the gate. Weekends and holidays can sell out. The official site can reject some foreign cards; Klook is a reliable fallback.

name: Tokyo DisneySea
kidNotes: More adult-leaning than Disneyland, but Fantasy Springs and Mermaid Lagoon are made for little ones.
summary: Widely called the most beautiful theme park in the world — volcanic lagoons, Venetian canals and the Fantasy Springs expansion.

booking.howTo: Same release as Disneyland: 60 days ahead at 2 PM Japan time, online only — no tickets at the gate.

name: teamLab Planets
nameLocal: チームラボプラネッツ
kidNotes: Barefoot, knee-deep water rooms — kids love it. Wear shorts or roll-up trousers.
summary: An immersive digital art museum you walk through barefoot — koi swimming around your ankles, a floating flower garden and a universe of light.
tncTip: Book the very first slot of the day. It's calm, the mirrors are empty, and you're out before the lunchtime rush.

booking.howTo: No fixed release date — tickets come out in batches roughly 2–3 months ahead. Book 3–4 weeks out for weekends and holidays. No tickets at the door.

name: teamLab Borderless
nameLocal: チームラボボーダレス
kidNotes: Dark, maze-like rooms — hold small hands. The Athletics Forest is a favourite for 4+.
summary: A borderless world of art that drifts between rooms — the sister to Planets, more mysterious and dreamlike.

booking.howTo: No fixed release date — tickets come out in batches a couple of months ahead. Book a few weeks out for weekends and holidays.

name: Shibuya Sky
kidNotes: Children’s tickets can’t be bought online: book the adults online, then buy the kids’ tickets at the 14th-floor counter on the day. Open-air rooftop with high glass walls. No loose items (hats, bags) on the roof — lockers provided.
priceNote: Adult web ticket before 3 PM (¥3,400 after). Children’s tickets (to age 12, ¥1,200) are sold only at the 14th-floor counter
summary: An open-air rooftop 230m above the Shibuya scramble — the definitive Tokyo sunset, with Mt Fuji on clear days.
tncTip: Sunset slots go first. Book the slot that starts ~40 minutes before sunset so you see daylight, golden hour and the city lighting up.

booking.howTo: Adult web tickets open two weeks ahead at midnight Japan time, and sunset slots can vanish within hours. Children’s tickets are counter-only, so a child can’t be booked online.

name: Ghibli Museum
nameLocal: 三鷹の森ジブリ美術館
kidNotes: Under-4s free. The Catbus room is for children 12 and under only — little ones adore it.
summary: Hayao Miyazaki's whimsical museum — a short film you can only see here, the life-size Catbus and the rooftop Robot Soldier.

booking.howTo: The entire next month releases on the 10th at 10:00 AM JST via Lawson Ticket and sells out in minutes. Tickets are named — bring matching ID.

name: Pokémon Café Tokyo
kidNotes: Pikachu comes out to dance — ask for a table with a view of the stage.
summary: Pikachu-shaped curry, Gengar desserts and a live Pikachu show — the most sought-after table in Tokyo for Pokémon fans.

booking.howTo: Reservations open 31 days ahead at 6:00 PM JST and go in seconds. Have the page open early; retry ~6:15 PM for cancellations.

name: Kirby Café Tokyo
summary: Impossibly cute Kirby-shaped food in Skytree Town — pairs perfectly with the Sumida Aquarium.

booking.howTo: The following month opens on the 10th at 6:00 PM JST. Popular slots go within a minute.

name: Warner Bros. Studio Tour Tokyo — The Making of Harry Potter
kidNotes: Big walking day — bring the stroller. Robes and wands for small wizards in the shop.
summary: The Great Hall, Diagon Alley and the Hogwarts Express — the largest indoor Harry Potter attraction in the world.

booking.howTo: Timed entry; weekends and special events sell out weeks ahead.

name: Sanrio Puroland
nameLocal: サンリオピューロランド
kidNotes: Indoor, stroller-friendly and perfectly pitched for under-6s.
summary: Hello Kitty's indoor theme park — shows, gentle rides and a lot of pink. A rainy-day saviour.

name: Sumida Aquarium
kidNotes: Compact and stroller-easy. The penguin pool is at toddler eye level.
summary: A jewel-box aquarium at the foot of Skytree — an open penguin pool and glowing jellyfish rooms.

name: Tokyo Skytree
summary: Japan's tallest tower, with a glass floor that tests every parent's nerves.

name: Kimono photoshoot at Senso-ji
kidNotes: Most studios dress children from age 2–3. Ask for a family package with hair styling.
summary: Tokyo's oldest temple, the Kaminarimon lantern and Nakamise street — best captured in kimono with a professional photographer.
tncTip: Book a family photo plan that includes dressing and hair — it takes the stress out of getting four people (two of them tiny) ready.

name: Akihabara
kidNotes: Arcades are loud and some upper floors are adults-only — stick to ground floors and big-name stores with kids.
summary: Electric Town — figures, retro games, multi-storey arcades and Mandarake's maze of collectibles.
tncTip: Go mid-morning on a weekday. Super Potato for retro games, Radio Kaikan for figures, and Sega/GiGO arcades for UFO catchers.

name: Unicorn Gundam & Gundam Base
nameLocal: ユニコーンガンダム立像
summary: A life-size, transforming Unicorn Gundam outside DiverCity, and the Gundam Base flagship store inside.
tncTip: Check the transformation schedule on the day and be in place a few minutes early; stay for the evening light show if the kids are still going.

name: Harajuku & Omotesando
kidNotes: Takeshita Street is a squeeze by noon — carrier over stroller.
summary: Takeshita Street's crêpes and kawaii fashion, then the tree-lined boulevard of Omotesando for sneakers and @cosme skincare.

name: Shibuya, the Crossing & Pokémon Center
summary: Shibuya 109 and Parco for fashion, Pokémon Center and Nintendo Tokyo upstairs at Parco, then the world's busiest scramble crossing.

name: Esogie — Nigerian dinner in Tokyo
summary: Jollof, egusi and a taste of home — our way of closing the trip.
tncTip: Small restaurant — reserve ahead, especially for a family of four.

name: Narita Express (N'EX)
kidNotes: Big luggage racks and reserved seats — the calmest way in with tired kids.
summary: The direct airport train from Narita to Tokyo, Shinjuku and Shibuya — all reserved seats.

name: Shinkansen Tokyo ⇄ Kyoto
kidNotes: Under-6s ride free on a lap; book them a seat if you want the row. Sit on the right (seat E) Tokyo→Kyoto for Mt Fuji.
summary: The bullet train between Tokyo and Kyoto in about 2h15m — reserve a full row, grab an ekiben, and watch for Fuji.
tncTip: Book through smartEX for the lowest fares — Hayatoku discounts apply if you book 7 or 21 days ahead. Reserve seats with oversized-luggage space if you're not forwarding bags.

booking.howTo: Seats can be reserved up to a year ahead on smartEX. Book 21+ days out for Hayatoku 21 fares.

name: Kiyomizu-dera
kidNotes: Steep approach — a carrier beats a stroller here.
summary: The wooden stage hanging over a sea of autumn maples — Kyoto's most iconic temple.
tncTip: 'Early' means 8:00. Tour buses land around 9:30 and the stage jams by 10:30.

name: Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka
summary: Stone-stepped lanes of teahouses and craft shops winding down from Kiyomizu-dera.

name: Yasaka Shrine
summary: The vermilion gateway to Gion, lit with hundreds of lanterns at night.

name: Gion at dusk
kidNotes: Some private lanes ban photography — look for the signs and keep it respectful.
summary: Hanamikoji and Shirakawa's willow-lined canal as the lanterns come on.

name: Nishiki Market
kidNotes: Narrow and busy — eating while walking is discouraged, so stop at stalls with standing space.
summary: 'Kyoto's Kitchen' — tamagoyaki, mochi, pickles and matcha everything along a covered lane.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
summary: Towering green stalks creaking in the wind — magical when empty.
tncTip: Empty at 8:00, a river of people by 10:00. Walk it first, then step straight into Tenryu-ji.

name: Tenryu-ji Temple garden
summary: A UNESCO-listed Zen garden borrowing the Arashiyama mountains as its backdrop — opens at 8:30.

name: Kimono rental in Arashiyama
kidNotes: Children's kimono from ~90cm. Pack a spare pair of socks — tabi and puddles don't mix.
summary: Dress the whole family and shoot by the Kimono Forest, the Togetsukyo bridge and the Nonomiya lanes.

name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
kidNotes: You don't need to summit — the first 20–30 minutes of gates are the most photogenic.
summary: Thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mt Inari — open 24 hours and free.
tncTip: Arrive by 7:30 — it's five minutes from Kyoto Station on the JR Nara line, and you can ride the same line on to Nara afterwards.

name: Nintendo Museum
nameLocal: ニンテンドーミュージアム
summary: Nintendo's own museum in Uji — 130 years of play, from hanafuda cards to giant interactive controllers.

rule.note: Leftover tickets may be sold first-come after the lottery.

booking.howTo: Tickets are allocated by lottery about three months ahead; any remaining tickets go on general sale later. Requires a Nintendo Account.

name: Tea ceremony in Kyoto
kidNotes: Choose a family-friendly class (45–60 min) where kids can whisk their own matcha.
summary: A quiet hour learning the way of tea — whisking matcha and wagashi sweets in a traditional tea room.

name: Universal Studios Japan & Super Nintendo World
nameLocal: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
kidNotes: Under-4s free. Mario Kart has a height minimum of 107cm; Yoshi's Adventure suits little ones.
summary: Mario Kart, Donkey Kong Country and Hogwarts in one park. Super Nintendo World needs timed entry — an Express Pass guarantees it.

booking.howTo: Studio Passes and Express Passes are released ~3 months ahead, one date at a time. Express Passes with Super Nintendo World timed entry sell out first.

name: Pokémon Café Osaka
nameLocal: ポケモンカフェ 大阪
summary: The Osaka sister café inside Daimaru Shinsaibashi — often a touch easier to book than Tokyo.

booking.howTo: Same system as Tokyo: 31 days ahead at 6:00 PM JST.

name: Dotonbori
kidNotes: Busiest and loudest after dark — go in the early evening, and a carrier is easier than a stroller in the crowds.
summary: Neon canals, the Glico running man, takoyaki and Don Quijote for a tax-free skincare haul.

name: Shinsaibashi & Amerimura
summary: A 600m covered shopping arcade, then Osaka's streetwear and sneaker district next door.

name: Osaka Castle Park
summary: The gold-trimmed castle keep above moats and gingko trees blazing yellow in late autumn.

name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
kidNotes: Spirals down around a giant central tank — whale sharks at stroller height.
summary: One of the world's great aquariums, built around a nine-metre-deep Pacific tank with whale sharks.

name: Nara Park & Todai-ji
kidNotes: Deer bow for crackers — and nibble once they're gone. Let kids hand them over quickly, then show empty palms.
summary: Bowing deer and the 15-metre Great Buddha inside one of the world's largest wooden buildings.
tncTip: Feed the deer early, before they're overfed and grumpy. Inside Todai-ji, small kids can crawl through the pillar 'Buddha's nostril' for good luck.

name: NARUTO & BORUTO Shinobi-Zato
kidNotes: Some ninja trials have age/height limits — the easier missions suit 5+ with a parent.
summary: Ninja trials through a hidden-leaf village, Ichiraku Ramen and the Hokage Rock — inside Awaji's Nijigen no Mori anime park.
tncTip: Get there for opening and do this first while energy is high, then ease into the Crayon Shin-chan park after lunch.

booking.howTo: Buy online in advance for smoother entry; premium ticket bundles are limited.

name: Crayon Shin-chan Adventure Park
nameLocal: クレヨンしんちゃん アドベンチャーパーク
kidNotes: Kid-scaled obstacle courses and ziplines — the highlight for our 3- and 5-year-old.
summary: Outdoor adventure courses themed on the beloved anime family — built for small adventurers.

name: Godzilla Interception Operation Awaji
kidNotes: Zipline into Godzilla's mouth has weight/height limits; the life-size Godzilla is the photo for little ones.
summary: A life-size Godzilla, a zipline straight into its jaws, and a Godzilla museum. Dragon Quest Island next door is the alternative.

name: Hakone day trip
kidNotes: The ropeway over volcanic Owakudani and the pirate ship on Lake Ashi are pure joy for kids.
summary: Pirate ships, a volcanic ropeway, black eggs and — on clear days — Mt Fuji over Lake Ashi.

name: Mt Fuji & Lake Kawaguchiko
summary: Fuji reflected in the lake, the Chureito Pagoda and autumn leaves — easiest as a guided bus day trip with kids.
